traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report contains multiple studies: (1) an initial validation study (2 successive dilutions) with its own relative trueness table (per-category numeric SD/bias/CI not fully visible in extracted pages, only a narrative summary of out-of-limit samples was found on p.16), (2) an interlaboratory study with pooled accuracy-profile data by contamination level (not by category), and (3) an extension study using 'one plate and one dilution' interpretation (2025) whose per-category relative trueness table (Table 17, p.37) was fully visible and is the one recorded here, since it is the most complete and explicit per-category quantitative table found with n, SD, bias, LCL, UCL. A parallel 'Two Plates' column with nearly identical results (from the initial validation study) was also present in Table 17 but omitted here to avoid duplication - those values were: Meat 0.22/-0.09/-0.54/0.36; Dairy 0.35/-0.12/-0.86/0.62; Seafood 0.16/0.02/-0.32/0.36; Vegetal 0.12/-0.08/-0.34/0.18; Pastries&egg 0.38/-0.04/-0.86/0.78; Pet food 0.23/-0.26/-0.76/0.24. A third extension study using the Petrifilm Plate Reader Advanced (PPRA) also exists (section 8) but its per-category numeric table was not captured in the provided pages. The Acceptability Limit of ±0.5 log was explicitly stated multiple times (e.g. accuracy profile studies, interlaboratory study) and applied consistently across all study variants.
